No public school within 6 miles of family home. People best opportunity in life is to become a farmer as he and his relatives have a large body of excellent farm land and splendid cattle range. The education should encourage him in the direction of, rather than away from, the farm. I recommend the transfer of the said child. This 7th day of Sept., 1916 [signature] Agent or Superintendent. I therefore recommend that the said child be enrolled in this school. This 4th day of December, 1919 [signature] School Physician. SPECIAL NOTE. This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent should send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided by law. All the blanks must be filled in even if blank. If the information calls for any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unfilled. Whether the parents are living or dead, their names must be given. The person who signs the blank as consenting to the transfer should indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of kin," leaving unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. INDORSEMENTS. The laws relating to the transfer of Indian children from reservations and schools are as follows: That hereafter no Indian child shall be sent from any Indian reservation to a school beyond the State or Territory in which said reservation is situated without the voluntary consent of the father or mother of such child if either of them are living, and if neither of them are living without the voluntary consent of the next of kin of such child. Such consent shall be made before the agent of the reservation, and he shall send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate that such consent has been voluntarily given before such child shall be removed from such reservation. And it shall be unlawful for any Indian agent or other employee of the Government to induce, or seek to induce, by withholding rations or by other improper means, the parents or next of kin of any Indian to consent to the removal of any Indian child beyond the limits of any reservation. (28 Stats., p. 906.) Provided, That hereafter no Indian child shall be taken from any school in any State or Territory to a school in any other State against its will or without the written consent of its parents. (29 Stats., p. 348.) That no Indian pupil under the age of fourteen years shall be transported at Government expense to any Indian school beyond the limits of the State or Territory in which the parents of such child reside or of the adjoining State or Territory. (35 Stat. L., 781.) The rules provide that— A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. An Indian boy or girl 18 years old and over may, without the consent of parents or others, personally sign the application form on its being changed to suit the case—but in all cases where the parents are living they should first be consulted. This form is to be used only in transfers from reservations or Indian schools to nonreservation schools. NAME Willy Love Tribe {Full} Nez Perce State Idaho Dec. 4, 1919 Sex Male. VACATION REQUEST FOR PUPIL. We, the undersigned, respectfully request that leave of absence be granted ............................................ Willie Dave ............................................ from June 15, 1918 to Sept. 5, 1918 to enable him to visit his home. We hereby agree to pay all expenses, including round-trip railroad fares, sleeping-car fares, meals, lodging, stage fares, telegraph and telephone messages, and other incidental expenses connected with the visit. We further agree that said pupil shall be returned to the Cushman school on or before the last day of the leave of absence. We further agree to deposit with the superintendent of the school sufficient money to defray all expenses to be incurred, and should the pupils, or any one of them, fail to return to school at such time as may be agreed upon by the parents or guardian and the superintendent of the school in which the pupils are enrolled, the amount of money remaining with the superintendent, necessary to the return transportation of the pupil or pupils so neglecting to return, shall be forfeited to the Government; provided, however, that in all cases where it can be shown that there were justifiable reasons for the failure of the return of the pupil the forfeiture of the funds shall not take place. If the pupil neglecting to return is from a reservation, the superintendent of the reservation shall certify to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. If a pupil's home is not on a reservation, then the certificate of some reputable, disinterested citizen of the community may be requested as to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. Witness to mark, Ernest Wiley By [signature] Pratote Father. Mother. Guardian. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Colville Agency, Nespelem, Wash., Jan. 5, 1917. Mr. T.B. Wilson, Supt., Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Dear Mr. Wilson: Big Dave, the father of Willie Dave, was in the office today inquiring about his son Willie. He said that he had not heard from him in about two months and seemed to be uneasy about his health. Will you please write him a letter, or have his son Willie do so at an early date to let him know how he is. He said he sent his son some papers recently and they were returned. Yours respectfully, [signature] Superintendent. W.E.G.H. P.S. His address is Big Dave, Nespelem, Wash. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington. January 9, 1917. Big Dave, Nespelem, Washington. Dear Sir: At the request of Superintendent Johnson, I am writing you today relative to your son William Dave. William is getting along nicely in school at the present time and his health is good. I will have William write you a letter. I do not understand why the papers which you sent to your son were returned to you, unless it is possible that they might not have been correctly addressed. The correct address is, Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Washington. Very respectfully, [signature] Superintendent. 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Colville Agency, Nespelem, Washington. April 18, 1917. FOR FILE Supt. T. B. Wilson, Tacoma, Washington. Dear Sir: Herewith is check No. 726 in your favor for $15.00, transferring money to you for account of William Dave. Please use this to return the boy to his home, advising me when he will leave the school. Very respectfully, J. Johnson Superintendent. Sm Enc To go Monday Eve G. N. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Colville Agency, Nespelem, Wash. March 15, 1917 Mr. T. B. Wilson, Supt. Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. My dear Mr. Wilson: Willie Dave writes his father that he is sick and has been confined to the hospital for several days and, as is usual in such cases, he apparently has a stroke of homesickness and wishes to come back. Kindly advise me just what Willie's condition is at the present time and if in your opinion his condition is such as to justify his return home. If he is well I suggest that Willie be induced to write a more cheerful letter home. Has Willie any spending money? If not, I will arrange to transfer a small amount which will probably serve to keep him in better spirits. Very respectfully, J. M. Johnson Superintendent. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington. March 19, 1917. Mr. J. M. Johnson, Supt., Colville Agency, Nespelem, Washington. Dear Sir: I am in receipt of your letter of March 15, with reference to Willie Dave and I have to report that Willie was engaged in a wrestling match and got very warm from which he took a deep cold and had a slight attack of pneumonia, but he is now up and around and getting along nicely. The Doctor thinks he will be able to return to school in a few days if the weather is warm. Every precaution will be taken to protect his health and I think Willie will be alright in a short time. Very respectfully, TBW.C Superintendent. Nespelem Washington April 12, 1917 My Dear Friend: Mr. D.B. Wilson. Sept. today I was speaking to J.M. Johnson. I heard that Cushman Grade School will close at Apr. 15th, 1917 so I want to know that sq. lease tell me when it is to be closed and if the school is going to close at 15th April and will there come home. J.M. Johnson said that school will be at June, and tell me when it will be closed and where how I think I have to be at school or sick. And who is all for you so all men be truly and I received letter from Alice Dave he said that school will be closed at 15th of April. So good bye. From your friend, Mr. Dave Pistotse. Nespelem Washington. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington. April 14, 1917. Mr. Dave Pistotse, Nespelem, Washington. Dear Sir: In answer to your letter of April 12, I wish to say that this school will close on April 15, and your children will be permitted to go home at that time, if you wish them to. We have plenty of supplies of every kind to keep the children through the summer if they wish to stay, but we have no money to pay the teachers and have to close the school for this year. School will open again next year on September 10, and I hope you will send William back to school at that time. He can go home any time that you send the money to pay his railroad fare. I wrote to Big Dave several days ago telling him to send money for William's fare. Very respectfully, Superintendent. CASE RECORD.
